note: Slight up lean: the street's Q4/FY bar already sits about 10% below the company's $1.1B, and an 18.8%-of-float short is building after a 55% fall. Against that, the DSP shortage, the memory drag and a sector that sells good prints (Coherent, Innolight) largely offset it on an 18% implied move.

Rests on primary documents: the company beat its own sales guide in Q1 and Q2, and Q3 consensus sits exactly on the flat guide. Peer toy prints are strong, a raise would mechanically lift the low end of the FY guide, and an activist holds about 23% with a rising short behind it. Small offsets from Pop Mart and the absence of a tariff refund.

Modest up lean. Revenue has beaten consensus by 8-11% and consensus has Q3 flat on Q2, while Hinge reported a record selling season. The size is held down because beat-and-raise prints have been sold twice in three, H2 EBITDA is guided lower, and GLP-1 coverage is ambiguous.

Peer documents support a faded outbreak drag and a soft FY guide: CAVA raised its FY same-restaurant-sales guide on an outbreak drag of only ~150bp, and Chipotle's comps recovered by August. The lean is cut back because of the 130% rally, spot sitting above the average target, call-heavy positioning, four straight revenue misses and 5 of 7 prints sold.

Up lean on a 42%-of-float short at the 52-week low and on a stale ~$62M headline consensus that LivePerson's 27 days in the quarter will appear to beat. It is largely offset by the risk that the first combined guide lands below a FY27 Street near $390M; the bar is disputed and the call skew has already paid for some upside.
